messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: SERVICE ALERT: Elevated 5xx + timeouts observed from private VPC egress to inference-gateway-prod. Trigger: 5xx rate > 8% for 3m, latency spikes. Paging oncall.
anna: Oncall here, ack. Visible in dashboard — spikes started ~5m ago. Any customer-facing titan? :eyes:
lisa: Support: getting pings from Customer:FinA (eu-west1) and AdPlatform (us-east) reporting request timeouts and HTTP 504s. Raising high severity from their side.
miguel: I'm on triage. Pulling NAT gateway/egress metrics and conntrack counts. First glance, NAT ephemeral port utilization high and a small burst of connection resets to infra egress IPs.
jamie: NetEng hopping in — looking at peering and SGs. No recent SG rollouts in prod according to rollout dashboard.
miguel: Logs: ```
# nat-metrics
nat_gateway.ephemeral_utilization=92%
nat_gateway.5xx_rate=0.12
conntrack.entries=199900
conntrack.size=200000
``` 
miguel: conntrack is near capacity (+logs show dropped packets). That can cause asymmetric responses and 504s when NAT can't allocate SNAT.
anna: Can we confirm if this is NAT gateway autoscaling failing or an app-side connection storm? Any recent batch jobs hitting external endpoints?
lisa: Customer reports spike correlates with an hourly sync job they kicked off at :10 UTC.
miguel: That explains the sudden surge. We're seeing long-lived outbound connections + many short ones — classic ephemeral port exhaustion.
jamie: On peering: BGP stable, no route flaps. No transit appliance errors. SGs look ok. This is likely NAT-side.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3521, paging SRE+NetEng. Incident channel: #incidents/3087654321
miguel: Quick mitigations we can attempt now:
- recycle NAT allocation on affected subnet (causes short disruption)
- add temporary extra NAT instance behind gateway (provider API)
- implement source-based route to fall back to host-egress (hosted egress) for impacted prefixes
I'm pushing provider scale-up now.
jamie: While that scales, we can reduce ephemeral pressure by enforcing keepalive/timeouts on backend pools and short-lived retries. Can ops-team coordinate a throttle with customer support?
lisa: Messaging customers now: telling them we're investigating and throttling is in progress. ETA for mitigation 10-15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
miguel: Provider api returns: scale action accepted, launching +2 nat instances into pool. Conntrack resets dropping now, ephemeral util trending down to 78%.
anna: Good. Any secondary work to avoid recurrence? We should add per-customer egress quotas and alert on ephemeral utilization per-VPC.
jamie: Agree. Also we should add NAT translation headroom alarms and automatic scale policies for these private VPCs. I'll file followups.
miguel: Temporary live mitigation we applied:
1) provider scale +2 NATs (complete)
2) rerouted AdPlatform prefixes to alternate gateway via routing override
3) applied conntrack timeout reduces on NAT instances to free stale entries: ```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300``` 
Early results: 5xx rate dropping 8% -> 1.6%, p50 latency back to baseline.
lisa: Customer update sent: FinA sees requests succeed again, AdPlatform still had a small window where retries failed but now OK.
anna: Assigning incident lead to miguel. Jamie, please own networking follow-up. Lisa, own customer comms. I'll take postmortem.
miguel: Putting notes in INC-2026-3521. Will capture root cause hypothesis: customer sync + no NAT autoscale headroom -> conntrack exhaustion -> dropped SNAT allocations -> gateway 504s.
jamie: Follow-ups I'm planning:
- review NAT autoscale policy and min capacity
- add per-VPC ephemeral port utilization alarms
- evaluate moved-to-hosted fallback automation for sudden spikes
I'll tag infra and platform teams.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary reroute initiated for 10% of traffic for impacted customers to hosted-egress. ```/reroute start --service inference-gateway --target hosted-egress --percent 10 --reason "mitigate nat exhaustion"``` 
deploy-bot: Canary at 10% stable. No regressions.
miguel: Last checks: conntrack entries 120k/200k, nat util 54%, 5xx rate 0.8% over last 2m. Sounds stable.
anna: Excellent. Lowering page to watch-only. Keeping incident open for followups and postmortem.
lisa: Final customer notes: both customers marked as degraded for 00:06-00:20 UTC window, full recovery confirmed at :20 UTC. Will attach customer timeline to ticket.
miguel: I'll seed a short runbook excerpt for oncall: "If ephemeral_util >85% and conntrack > 90%: scale NAT + reduce conntrack timeout + consider reroute to hosted-egress" and push to ops-runbooks.
jamie: Creating followup ticket NET-776 to adjust autoscale and alarms.
anna: Thanks team. Handoff to primary SRE shift begins in 20m; I'll post summary to #oncall-handoff and assign to next oncall.
ops-bot: Incident severity reduced to P2. Postmortem scheduled. :thumbsup:
